Grammar in Context

Mauritania: A Country of Contrasts

Comparative Adjectives

Read the text and choose the correct answer (A, B or C) for each gap.

Mauritania is a large country in West Africa. Much of the country is covered by the Sahara Desert, so many parts of Mauritania are (1) ___ than places near the coast.

The capital, Nouakchott, is one of the biggest cities in the country. It is (2) ___ than many other towns in Mauritania and has more shops, schools and services.

One of Mauritania’s most unusual forms of transport is its famous iron ore train. The train is (3) ___ than most ordinary passenger trains and can be several kilometres long.

The journey across the desert can also be (4) ___ than a normal train journey. Passengers may spend many hours travelling through hot and dusty areas.

Life near the Atlantic coast can feel (5) ___ than life deep in the desert because temperatures are often less extreme there.

  1. A. dryB. drierC. driest
  2. A. busyB. busierC. busiest
  3. A. longB. longerC. longest
  4. A. difficultB. more difficultC. most difficult
  5. A. comfortableB. more comfortableC. most comfortable
View Answers
  1. B — drier
  2. B — busier
  3. B — longer
  4. B — more difficult
  5. B — more comfortable

Rodents: Nature’s Busy Helpers

Present Simple

Read the text and choose the correct answer (A, B or C) for each gap.

Rodents are a fascinating group of mammals. This group (1) ___ mice, squirrels, beavers and capybaras. They come in many shapes and sizes, and each species has its own way of life.

One special feature connects them all: their front teeth (2) ___ growing throughout their lives. Gnawing on food and other materials helps keep these teeth at a useful length.

In autumn, a squirrel often (3) ___ nuts and seeds in the ground for later. It (4) ___ always find every hidden seed again. Some of those seeds grow into new trees, so squirrels help forests renew themselves.

Beavers are talented builders. They (5) ___ branches and mud to build dams across streams. The ponds behind these dams provide homes for frogs, insects and water birds. A beaver’s hard work benefits many neighbours!

Capybaras, the world’s largest living rodents, usually (6) ___ in groups near water. They are excellent swimmers. A capybara (7) ___ much of its day eating grasses or resting, and water offers a place to cool down.

How (8) ___ these animals help the natural world? From planting future trees to creating wetland habitats, rodents play many useful roles. Learning about them gives us more reasons to appreciate the wildlife around us.

  1. A. includeB. includingC. includes
  2. A. keepB. keepsC. keeping
  3. A. hideB. hidesC. hiding
  4. A. don’tB. isn’tC. doesn’t
  5. A. useB. usesC. using
  6. A. livesB. liveC. living
  7. A. spendB. spendingC. spends
  8. A. doB. doesC. are
View Answers
  1. C — includes
  2. A — keep
  3. B — hides
  4. C — doesn’t
  5. A — use
  6. B — live
  7. C — spends
  8. A — do
